rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow Roberts opinion vacating and remanding, grounding the result in rigorous Rule 23(b)(3) predominance/superiority (and TransUnion’s “standing to recover”) where the certification model sweeps in many uninjured members without an administrable classwide winnowing method. Separate writings are most likely from Kagan (dissent emphasizing TransUnion’s reserved timing issue and workable screening) and Thomas (concurrence pressing a more structural Article III/Rules Enabling Act view of certification’s constitutional limits).
